title: Deformation space of a closed section
statement:
Use the coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions] and the situation of [def-pur-section-invariant]: $B,V$ are finite-type $k$-schemes, $g:V\to B$ is smooth, separated and of finite type, and $s:B\hookrightarrow V$ is a closed section, $g\circ s=\mathrm{id}_B$. No constant relative dimension is imposed. Affine space is [def-sbc-affine-space], and fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]. The deformation to the normal cone of the section is the actual scheme
$$
D_sV=\operatorname{Bl}_{s(B)\times\{0\}}(V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B)
\setminus\widetilde{V\times_B\{0\}},
$$
where the blow-up is [def-nagata-global-blowup] and the tilde is the scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform], not just a topological closure. Write $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_V\to s_*\mathcal O_B)$ for the ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$, with $I=\mathcal I(U)$, the inverse image of $U$ in $D_sV$ is
$$
\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t],\qquad R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}],
$$
the subalgebra generated by $R[t]$ and all $f/t$ with $f\in I$. The spectrum and its contravariant maps are [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These charts specify the maps
$$
\widetilde g:D_sV\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B,\qquad
\widetilde s:\mathbf A^1_B\longrightarrow D_sV:
$$
$\widetilde g$ is the blow-up projection followed by projection to $\mathbf A^1_B$, and $\widetilde s$ is induced on the displayed chart by the augmentation $R[t,I/t]\to(R/I)[t]$, $r\mapsto\bar r$, $t\mapsto t$, $f/t\mapsto0$. They satisfy $\widetilde g\circ\widetilde s=\mathrm{id}$; $\widetilde g$ is smooth separated of finite type and $\widetilde s$ is a closed immersion [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $\omega_{\widetilde g}=R\widetilde g^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_B}$ as in [def-pur-section-invariant]. The family object is the actual derived pullback
$$
F=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}
=C(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)
\in\operatorname{Pic}\bigl(D^b_{ctf}(\mathbf A^1_B,\Lambda)\bigr).
$$
The derived operations and the Picard groupoid have precisely the meaning of [def-pur-section-invariant]; in particular this asserts tensor invertibility and finite Tor amplitude, with no chosen orientation. At finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ this is the finite family; the other coefficient stages use exactly the transports of [def-pur-conventions]. Here $\Lambda_T$ is the coefficient unit of [def-pur-conventions]: $A_T$ at finite level, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ at integral level, and its rationalized or common-stage image at field levels. The integral bounded-constructible and finite-Tor conditions use single intervals uniform in all finite reductions, as specified there.

proof.text: Construct the blow-up and its strict transform using [def-nagata-global-blowup] and [def-nagata-strict-transform]. The gluing datum [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data] uses exactly the affine blow-ups specified in [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model], so computations on these local models compute the global object. The closure in the strict-transform definition is the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure], cut out by the kernel ideal sheaf by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. Finite-type $k$-schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: a field has only the ideals $0,k$, so is Noetherian. Use a finite affine cover with Noetherian coordinate rings as in [pqf-def-locnoeth]; its ideals are finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The center $s(B)\times\{0\}$ is a closed immersion into $V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B$; on affine charts its quotient is by the finitely generated ideal $(I,t)$, so it is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. It is affine and quasi-compact by [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], hence a finite-presentation center in the convention of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], as required by the strict-transform definition. For such a chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $V$ put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, the ideal of its closed section from [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Over $U$ the blow-up center has ideal $J=(I,t)\subseteq R[t]$. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] and [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], the $t$-chart is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$. The $f_i$-chart is $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/f_i][v]$, with $v=t/f_i$: this follows by substituting $t=f_iv$ in the subalgebra of $R_{f_i}[t]$. The strict transform of $t=0$ is empty in the $t$-chart, since $f=t(f/t)$ makes every $f\in I$ vanish modulo $t$, whereas away from the center some $f$ must be invertible. In the $f_i$-chart it is exactly $v=0$: put $C=R[I/f_i]$. In this chart $I C=(f_i)$, since $f=f_i(f/f_i)$, and $t=f_iv$. Thus the original closed fibre away from the center is $v=0$ with $f_i$ inverted, with ring $C_{f_i}$. It is a quasi-compact, quasi-separated immersion: it is a principal open in the closed subscheme $v=0$ of this affine chart. Its closure ideal is the kernel of $C[v]\to C_{f_i}$, $v\mapsto0$. The inclusion $C\subseteq R_{f_i}$ makes multiplication by $f_i$ injective on $C$, so this kernel is exactly $(v)$. These kernel ideals agree on open restrictions, giving the asserted scheme-theoretic closure. Its complement is $D(v)$, which is the overlap with the $t$-chart (the two homogeneous generators have invertible ratio). Thus removing the strict transform leaves exactly the $t$-chart over every $U$. The computation commutes with localization in $R$, so these are the affine charts of the actual blow-up open, not an object chosen merely for its fibres.

The projection to $\mathbf A^1_B$ is the restriction of the blow-up projection. Write $A=R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$. Every element has a unique finite Laurent expression $\sum_j a_jt^j$: uniqueness holds for Laurent polynomials over any ring, including rings with zero divisors. The coefficient condition for membership in $A$ is $a_j\in I^{-j}$ for $j<0$, with unrestricted coefficients for $j\geq0$. Indeed the generators have this property, it is preserved by products and sums, and each element of $I^r$ is a finite sum of products of $r$ elements of $I$. Define $\epsilon(\sum_j a_jt^j)=\sum_{j\geq0}\bar a_jt^j\in(R/I)[t]$. It is additive. For multiplicativity, a product term involving a negative exponent has a coefficient in $I$; if its resulting exponent is nonnegative it reduces to zero, and otherwise it is discarded. Terms involving only nonnegative exponents multiply by ordinary reduction modulo $I$. Thus $\epsilon$ is a ring map, sends every $f/t$ to zero, and is surjective because it contains all reduced constants and $t$. The affine-spectrum functor of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the surjective-ring-map criterion of [def-weil-closed-immersion] give $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)[t]\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$. These formulas agree after localizing $R$, hence agree on affine refinements of overlaps and glue to $\widetilde s$. The inverse image of each deformation chart is precisely $s^{-1}(U)\times\mathbf A^1$; these charts cover the target and their inverse images are affine. This proves closedness globally by the same affine criterion. The map fixes all base functions and $t$, so $\widetilde g\circ\widetilde s=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Definition: the displayed projection and section; explicit augmentation of the deformation algebra

proof.text: Construct etale coordinates of the pair near each point $s(b)$. By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], after restricting to affine neighbourhoods, $g$ factors as an etale map $e:W\to\mathbf A^d_{B'}$ followed by projection, with $b\in B'$ and $s(b)\in W$. Shrink $B'$ into $s^{-1}(W)$ so the whole restricted section lands in $W$. Subtract the $d$ coordinate functions of $e\circ s$; translation by these functions is an automorphism of affine space, so the translated etale map sends $s$ to the zero section. Put $P=W\times_{\mathbf A^d_{B'}}B'$. Its projection $P\to B'$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The map $e$ is separated: on the initial affine neighbourhoods it is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; restriction and base change restrict its closed diagonal. Thus $P\to B'$ is separated. The induced section $B'\to P$ is open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. Remove the other open-and-closed component of $P$ from $W$; it is closed in $W$, since $P$ is the inverse image of the closed zero section. After this restriction $e^{-1}(0)=s(B')$ as closed subschemes. Refine again around $s(b)$ to an affine open and shrink $B'$ to a principal affine neighbourhood in its inverse image under $s$; the restriction of that affine open is again principal affine, so both schemes remain affine. Such restrictions preserve etaleness by [def-weil-etale-morphism], since the condition is affine-local. We obtain affine coordinates $B'=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to R$ etale, with the actual section ideal $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)R$. Closedness and restriction here use precisely the affine quotient criterion of [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the diagonal definition of [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Clause (2), coordinates of the closed section; expanded using Stacks Tags 054L, 02GO, 024T, 01KT, 01S8

proof.text:
On a pair chart from step 3 put $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\subset C$. The standard deformation algebra $C[t,J/t]$ is $A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$, with $x_i=tu_i$: the polynomial homomorphism sends $u_i$ to $x_i/t$ and $t$ to $t$ and is surjective because $x_i=t(x_i/t)$. Injectivity follows already inside $A[t,t^{-1},x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, since different monomials $t^a u^\alpha$ map to different Laurent monomials $t^{a-|\alpha|}x^\alpha$; it does not require that $A$ be a domain. The etale map $e$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so $R$ is a flat $C$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the inclusion $C[t,J/t]\hookrightarrow C[t,t^{-1}]$. Its tensor with $R$ remains injective. The target identifies with $R[t,t^{-1}]$ by $r\otimes\sum c_jt^j\mapsto\sum rc_jt^j$, and the image is exactly the subalgebra generated by $R[t]$ and all $x_i/t$. Since $I=JR$, this image is $R[t,I/t]$. Hence the actual chart of our deformation is
$$\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]\simeq W\times_{\mathbf A^d_{B'}}\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_{B'}},$$
where the map to $\mathbf A^d_{B'}$ has coordinates $x_i=tu_i$. Its projection to $\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_{B'}}$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The affine-space projection is smooth of relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], so their composite is smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2), with the etale map having relative dimension zero as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Step 1's charts commute with restriction in $V$ and $B$, so these give smooth open neighbourhoods of every point over $t=0$: the identity $f=t(f/t)$ forces its image in $V$ to lie in $s(B)$. Away from $t=0$, the chart equality $R[t,I/t][t^{-1}]=R[t,t^{-1}]$ gives $V\times_B\mathbf G_{m,B}$, with smooth projection by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Smoothness is affine-local by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. These two sets of neighbourhoods prove smoothness globally, allowing the local integer $d$ to vary. No geometric DNC theorem or assertion about its family is used.

source.place: Clause (2), calculation x_i=t u_i; flat tensor injection and etale base change, Stacks Tags 00HD, 02GO, 01VA, 01VB

proof.text: The chart description also makes $h:D_sV\to V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B$ affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target]: the inverse image of $U\times\mathbf A^1=\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$. Each algebra is finitely generated over $R[t]$, with generators $f_1/t,\ldots,f_m/t$. Thus $h$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). The projection $p:V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ is separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to the stated $g$. The composite $\widetilde g=ph$ is of finite type: over each affine target choose finitely many affine charts for $p$, then finitely many for $h$ above those, and compose the finite sets of algebra generators. Its diagonal factors as the closed diagonal of $h$ followed by the base change of the closed diagonal of $p$; a base change of a surjective ring map is surjective, and a composition of surjections is surjective, so these maps are closed immersions by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is precisely separatedness in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Finally $\mathbf A^1_B$ and $D_sV$ are finite type over $k$: on a finite affine cover of $B$ use the polynomial algebra $R[t]$, and compose with the finite-type map just established. All domain hypotheses of the section-invariant definition are now verified.

source.place: Well-definedness of the displayed exceptional inverse image: separated finite-type domain

proof.text: Apply [def-pur-section-invariant] to the actual pair $(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)$ constructed in steps 1 and 2. Steps 3–5 give precisely its smooth, separated, finite-type and finite-type-over-$k$ hypotheses, and step 2 gives the closed section and its identity. Define $F$ to be that node's actual derived pullback $C(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)=L\widetilde s^*R\widetilde g^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_B}$. Its tensor-invertibility and membership in $D^b_{ctf}$ are exactly the final assertion of that node, including its specified higher coefficient stages. This supplies the claimed object of the Picard groupoid. No choice from an existence theorem is used in its underlying data, and no purity orientation is added. More explicitly, [def-pur-conventions] uses the small pro-etale site and the unit $A_T$, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$, or its rationalized/common-stage image at the respective coefficient stages. Its exceptional inverse image is defined for separated finite-type morphisms between finite-type $k$-schemes; steps 3–5 and the finite-type base $\mathbf A^1_B$ verify exactly that domain. No absolute separatedness of $B$ or $V$ is needed. At integral coefficients the boundedness and Tor intervals are uniform in all finite reductions. The conventions name operations only; the tensor-invertibility assertion used here comes from [def-pur-section-invariant], not from the conventions. No twist tensor comparison or exceptional-adjoint admissibility datum is used.

Statement: it is the blueprint's blow-up minus strict transform, with the maps g~, s~ and F in Pic(D^b_ctf(A^1_B,Lambda)). The setting and coefficient units are those of def-pur-section-invariant and def-pur-conventions; no constant relative dimension and no absolute separatedness is added, and nothing is weakened. Step 1: the center (I,t) is of finite presentation; the f_i-chart is C[v] with C=R[I/f_i] a subring of R_{f_i}; the strict-transform closure kernel is (v), which agrees with Stacks 080D's supported-sections quotient; the complement D(v) is the t-chart overlap, so D_sV is the union of the t-charts R[t,I/t]. Step 2: the Laurent membership criterion (a_j in I^{-j} for j<0) holds and the augmentation is a ring map; it is surjective, glues, is a closed immersion, and g~ s~ = id. Step 3: e is affine, hence separated, before the etale clopen-section lemma is applied; translation and removal of the other component give I=(x_i)R. Step 4: R is flat over C, so the inclusion stays injective after tensoring and its image is exactly R[t,I/t]; this is an etale base change of the A^d-projection, which is smooth; the zero fibre is covered via f=t(f/t), and the part with t invertible is smooth base change. Step 5: the separated finite-type checks are correct. Step 6: it specializes def-pur-section-invariant, whose statement asserts the inverse Q. Small cases tested: zero section of A^1_k (k[t,u], x=tu), s=id, components disjoint from the section, nonreduced B, varying d, empty schemes.
